tagline.text: The big island of the Calamian group beyond Coron, home to shipwrecks and a safari park

location.label: Location
location.text: Western Busuanga Island, Calamian Islands, Palawan (municipal seat at Salvacion)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱150–2,000 (basic items such as airport transfer and entrance fees, excluding tours and diving, confirm each item locally)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Busuanga Airport (Francisco B. Reyes Airport, USU)

children.text: The municipality of Busuanga covers the west of Busuanga Island, Calauit Island and other areas in northern Palawan. Coron town shares the eastern side of Busuanga Island. Calauit Safari Park, the Concepcion coast and wrecks, Black Island and Pass Island are stops on the Busuanga side.

Busuanga is an island in the Calamian Islands in northern Palawan, and also a municipality of the same name. The municipality covers the western third of Busuanga Island and Calauit Island. It is bounded by the Mindoro Strait to the north, Coron to the east, the South China Sea to the west and Culion Island to the south. The municipal seat is Salvacion, and the municipal motto is "The Last Shades of Paradise." What travelers usually call Coron is actually the town at the eastern end of the island, while the municipality of Busuanga itself is the quieter area to its west.
In the 2024 census the population was about 26,974, and the area is about
393km²
. Nearly half the land is brush and grassland and about 39% is forest, while Calauit Safari Park and the Yulo King Ranch together make up about 59% of the total area. The highest point is about

high, and the hills are largely limestone and chert. The rivers include the Busuanga and Binalayan rivers, and Concepcion Falls and Chinabayan (Sinabuyan) Falls are known. The dry season runs from December to May and the rainy season from June to November, with an average daily high of about
and a low of about
. The poverty incidence fell from about 70% in 2000 to 21.1% in 2023, and tourism, ranching and farming support the local economy.

The history is layered. Spanish rule reached the island in 1622 and Augustinian Recollect missionaries arrived, and in 1636 fortifications were built against raids. In 1904 nearby Culion Island became a government reservation for people with leprosy. In 1938 manganese deposits were found and a national road was built from Coron. In World War II Japanese forces occupied Coron and Busuanga, and on September 24, 1944 US bombers attacked Japanese ships anchored in Coron Bay and sank them. Those wrecks are today's dive sites. Busuanga was separated from Coron by Republic Act No. 560 in 1950 and became a municipality in 1951. The people and nature also deserve a look. Small islands around the island are home to the indigenous Tagbanua people, and seagrass beds are known as feeding grounds for dugongs and sea turtles. The municipality has 14 barangays, some of them on islands such as Panlaitan, where a LORAN navigation station operated after World War II until 1970. The terrain is largely chert, limestone and karst, giving a rugged coastline, and there are said to be three mineral springs. Beaches that travelers visit include the white sand and snorkeling at Pamalican Island, Las Hamacas Beach Resort, and the caves and white sand of Malajon (Black Island).

Compared with the island tours from Coron town, Busuanga as a destination feels much quieter and rougher. The famous lagoons and lakes are on the Coron Island side, while Busuanga offers African animals on Calauit Island, the coast and wrecks around Concepcion, and day-trip islands such as Black Island and Pass Island. Most accommodation and services are in Coron town, so this guide assumes you start in Coron and explore Busuanga from there. Fees and schedules differ between sources, so I have given ranges or "confirm locally" wherever possible.

blocks.title: The safari park on Calauit Island

children.text: The
Busuanga municipal guide
lists giraffes and zebras among the animals at Calauit Safari Park. Check hours, embarkation and admission with the local office or operator, and follow staff instructions.

blocks.title: Shipwrecks of Coron Bay and Concepcion

children.text: Japanese ships sunk in 1944 lie across Coron Bay. The Okikawa Maru is about
long and lies at 10–26 m, and the Akitsushima, a seaplane tender at 22–36 m, is known for its crane still standing. Concepcion is one of the bases closest to these wrecks, about
40km
from Coron town.

Concepcion Falls is an inland waterfall in tropical jungle. Some visitors found it smaller than expected, and the way there involves a bit of walking. One source says it takes about an hour by motorbike from Coron town and another says about an hour and a half, so allow plenty of time.

Black Island has limestone cliffs and soft sand and is described as a day trip farther away than the Coron Island sites. Pass Island is a day trip by boat along the coast from Concepcion, with a white sand beach lined with palms.
Mount Darala, the highest point on Busuanga Island at about
, is a tough hike that takes most of a day from Coron town. Go with a guide, and expect the trail to be muddy after rain.

blocks.title: Cheey village's small school and beach

children.text: Cheey is the largest barangay in Busuanga, taking up about 32% of the municipality's land. It has a small school built with the support of a tour operator and a beach, and it is described as a stop for meeting local villagers.
With a guide, a walk of about
45 minutes
through the forest leads to a river with swimming holes and a waterfall. The advice is to go with a local guide rather than alone.

items.title: A day from Coron
items.subtitle: A taste of the west of the island

children.text: Leave your hotel in Coron town. Use a pre-booked van or motorbike.
Head toward Concepcion. Look at the villages and coconut groves on the way, and allow plenty of time.
Walk to Concepcion Falls, or have lunch and rest on the coast.
From Concepcion, take a boat to an island such as Pass Island or Black Island for swimming and relaxing.
Return to Coron before dark.
Confirm boat fares and times locally before you go. They differ between reports.
Go from Coron to the northern pier. Calauit is a separate island, so you need a boat.
See giraffes and zebras at Calauit Safari Park.
Have lunch at the park or nearby.
Look around the nearby beaches and village, then return to Coron.
From Manila (MNL) to Busuanga Airport (Francisco B. Reyes Airport, USU) takes about
1 hour
. Check airline websites for timetables.
There are also routes from Cebu, Puerto Princesa and Boracay (Kalibo and Caticlan), but airline routes change over time.
If visiting Coron, check the Environmental Tourism Development Fee and payment terms through
Coron iPASS
. Confirm any separate fees for Busuanga attractions such as Calauit Safari Park directly.
Flights sell out early in peak season, so book ahead.

items.title: From the airport to Coron town

children.text: It is about
30–45 minutes
by car from the airport to Coron town, and some accounts mention unpaved sections.
Shared vans serve Coron Town hotels from the Busuanga airport arrivals area. If you booked a pickup, confirm where the driver will meet you. The
Busuanga transport guide
and recent local operator listings give different quotes, so confirm the per-person one-way fare.
The ferry or fast boat between El Nido and Coron takes about
4–8 hours
. Whether it runs depends on the weather, so check ahead.
An overnight ferry runs from Manila, but schedules are erratic and sailings are sometimes canceled. Keep spare time in your plans.
Use tricycles for nearby places such as Coron town and the hot springs.
For farther places, rent a motorbike for the day or join a minivan tour. Part of the road is unpaved, so a 4x4 may be needed.
Between islands, use a bangka.

The dry season in Busuanga runs from December to May and the rainy season from June to November. Diving guides treat October to May as the time when the sea is calmest and visibility best, with December to March as peak season. Visibility is about 10–20 m, and the water is about
year-round.
In the rainy season, especially July and August, gales and heavy rain can cause boats to be suspended and island tours to be canceled. Keep plenty of slack in your schedule then.

Almost all accommodation is in Coron town, and outside town one eco-resort up the coast is mentioned. In town, Corto del Mar in the center and The Funny Lion in a quiet outer area are mentioned in reports. To stay on the Busuanga side, look at dive bases near Concepcion or coastal resorts.
ATMs are only in Coron town, so carry enough cash. Internet is often slow or down, and a local SIM is said to be more reliable. For meals, local restaurants in Coron town offer the most choice.
ATMs are only in town, so withdraw plenty of cash before heading out to the islands.
For wreck diving, Advanced Open Water or higher is recommended, and penetrating the wrecks needs a separate certification.
Distant places make for long days, so plan an early start and return before sunset.
In the rainy season, leave slack in your schedule in case boats are canceled.
Ask your accommodation to arrange an airport pickup in advance.
Always take a guide for jungle walks and hikes.
The trails are muddy after rain, so bring suitable shoes.
A local SIM makes it easier to stay in touch.
In the afternoon, a sunset from Mount Tapyas in Coron town (about
, several hundred steps) or a soak in the Maquinit hot springs is a good way to end the day.
Don't try to see all of Busuanga at once. Split it into day trips to the west and the north. The island is large and the roads are poor, so travel takes a lot of time.
Island plans depend heavily on the weather, and flights sell out in peak season. Always check the latest announcements for flights and boats.
The wrecks are deep and penetrating them is dangerous, so go with a shop that has qualified and experienced staff.
Part of the road is unpaved and riding a motorbike carries a high risk of accidents. Bring insurance and a helmet.
Travelers report that there is no currency exchange at the airport, so bring the cash you need in advance.
The overnight ferry from Manila is erratic and sometimes canceled.
A base town about
30–45 minutes
by car from the airport, with accommodation and tours.
